newsitem.title: USA: Unisys seeks to reassure Fla. state workers.
newsitem.headline: Unisys seeks to reassure Fla. state workers.

text.p: Unisys Corp took out full-page ads in several Florida newspapers Monday reassuring state employees that the company was improving its processing of their health-care benefits.
Florida officials last week had accused the company of stonewalling a criminal investigation of an $86 million state insurance contract taken over by Unisys in January.

In January, Unisys took over a contract to process health care claims that Blue Cross/Blue Shield had previously managed. Since then, Unisys has been fined $1.7 million by state health-insurance regulators for slow payments and billing errors.
Unisys said Monday it has added customer service representatives, expanded service hours and updating the telephone system in an effort improve customer satisfaction.

In an open letter to members of the Florida Employees Group Health Self Insurance Plan posted in the Tallahassee Democrat newspaper, Unisys program director John Singleton said the company was working with government officials to improve much maligned services.

"The first few months have been challenging for all involved, but we have made considerable progress," Singleton said. "Unisys has committed significant additional resources to improve our ability to process your claims efficiently."
Unisys spokesoman Susan Beck said the company had taken out the advertisements, which she said she believed had appeared in eight Florida newspapers, to reach clients more quickly.
"We wanted to get it to them as fast as possible," she said.

Last week, Florida investigators criticized the Blue Bell, Pennsylvania-based company for supplying attorneys to Unisys employees being questioned in the probe, which is looking into how the company acquired the lucrative state contract.
Beck said the company was only following its own bylaws and Delaware law, which require that it provide legal assistance to employees being investigated for work-related actions.
